source: Facts from the Minecraft Wiki (minecraft.wiki: the mob, item and Tutorial pages), Java Edition, normal difficulty, written in our own words.

risky_food.chicken: raw chicken: 30% chance of Hunger, cook it first
risky_food.chorus_fruit: teleports you up to 8 blocks away

facts.fact: A zombie has 20 health and hits for about 3. It burns in daylight unless it's in water or shade or wears a helmet, and it has to wait between swings: step in right after it swings.
A husk is a desert zombie: it doesn't burn in the sun, and its hit makes you hungry.
Drowned live in water. One with a trident throws it from range, so don't swim at it in the open.
A skeleton has to draw its bow before it shoots: when the bow isn't drawn, no arrow is coming, so rush it then. A shield stops its arrows, and it burns in daylight. Skeletons run from wolves.

A creeper starts hissing when you're within 3 blocks and blows up a second and a half later. Get more than 7 blocks away and the fuse goes out. Hit it and back off, wait for the hiss to stop, then go in again. Creepers are scared of cats and ocelots.

An enderman is nearly 3 blocks tall: get under a roof 2 blocks high and it can't come in after you, while you hit its legs. Don't look at its face, and water hurts it. A carved pumpkin on your head lets you look at it safely.
A spider climbs walls and leaves you alone in bright light unless you hit it first. It fits through gaps one block high but not one block wide.
A cave spider is small enough to fit through one block, and its bite poisons. They come from spawners in mineshafts: break the spawner or put torches on it.
A witch throws potions of harming, poison, slowness and weakness, and drinks healing when hurt. Close in fast and hit while it's drinking.
Phantoms come at night once you haven't slept for three days. Sleeping in a bed stops them, and they burn in daylight.
A bed sets where you come back when you die. You can only sleep at night or in a thunderstorm, and not with monsters close by. A bed explodes in the Nether and the End.
Your health only comes back on its own when your hunger bar is nearly full. At 6 hunger or less you can't sprint, and at 0 you start taking damage.
Steak and cooked porkchop fill 8 hunger, the best common food. Cooked mutton, cooked chicken and cooked salmon fill 6, bread and baked potatoes 5. Raw meat is only 2 or 3.
Rotten flesh fills 4 hunger but usually makes you hungry: only eat it when there's nothing else.
A golden apple gives Regeneration II and Absorption: save it for a fight.
Swords hit for 4 (wood), 5 (stone), 6 (iron), 7 (diamond) and 8 (netherite), and swing fast.
An axe hits harder than a sword but swings slower: a stone axe hits for 9, a stone sword for 5. An axe also knocks a raised shield out for 5 seconds.
A shield takes 6 planks and 1 iron ingot. It blocks hits and arrows from the front, but an axe knocks it out for 5 seconds.
Each point of armor takes about 4% off a hit. A full set of iron gives 15 points, diamond 20.
A hit while falling (after a jump) is a critical hit, half as strong again. It doesn't work while sprinting.
Falling hurts 1 for every block past 3. Landing in water, or a water bucket placed just before you land, saves you.
Lava sets you on fire and hurts fast. Never dig straight down, and keep a bucket of water for lava.
You have about 15 seconds of air underwater, then you take 2 damage a second.
Monsters spawn in the dark (light level 0). A torch, a roof, a bed or just a good sword gets you through the night.

First day: about 10 logs, a crafting table, a wooden pickaxe, then around 19 cobblestone for a stone pickaxe, axe and sword. If dusk comes with no house, dig into a hill and block the hole behind you.
No house by night? Dig into a hillside and seal the way in, or use a village house: they often have a bed. Don't build with sand or gravel, they fall.
In a cave, put torches on your right going in: on the way out they're on your left. If you're really lost, dig a staircase up to the surface.
Sprinting burns hunger (0.1 a block, a sprint jump 0.2), walking burns none. Healing one health costs a lot, so eat food with high saturation: golden carrots 14.4, steak and porkchop 12.8.
Rabbit stew fills the most (10), then steak, cooked porkchop and pumpkin pie (8). For lasting full, golden carrots.
Diamonds are most common at the bottom of the world: mine at y -59, just over the bedrock, in a tunnel two high and one wide. Carry a water bucket: there's a lot of lava down there.
Mining in caves is quicker but riskier; a long tunnel two high and one wide is slower but safe. Never dig straight down or straight up.
Two blocks up and a zombie can't reach you while you hit it. Three or four up and you can hit a creeper before it blows.
A creeper is safest with a bow: about three shots. A shield blocks the whole blast, but it costs the shield a lot.
Don't sprint-hit a skeleton: the knockback just gives it room for a free shot.
Standing in water stops an enderman's attacks: it can't stand the water.
In the Nether, piglins leave you alone if you wear at least one piece of gold armor. Babies never attack.
Ghasts shoot from up to 100 blocks. Cobblestone stops their fireballs, and you can hit a fireball back at them.
Zombified piglins are calm, but hit one and the whole group comes for you.
Wither skeletons can't fit through a gap two blocks high, and their hit gives you Wither.
Blazes live in Nether fortresses. A fire resistance potion makes their fireballs harmless, and snowballs hurt them.
For the Nether bring iron armor and tools, a bow, plenty of food, cobblestone, flint and steel, and 10 obsidian for a way home. Water doesn't work there, and neither do compasses or beds.
Don't mine under sand or gravel: it falls on you and you can suffocate.
In a desert pyramid, don't dig down in the middle: there's a TNT trap under the pressure plate.
Never leave home without a water bucket: it puts out fire, turns lava to obsidian and breaks a fall.
Build walls high: spiders climb short ones, and players jump them.
Near a village at night, sleep: a zombie siege can start at midnight.
In PvP your reach is 3 blocks: hit from the edge of it. Swing when the bar is about 85% full, jump as you're hit to take less knockback, and let go of sprint before a jump-hit for a crit.
A sword does more damage over time (6.4 to 12.8 a second) than an axe (5.6 to 10); an axe hits harder once and breaks shields.
A bow is fully drawn in about a second and hits for 6. Punch knocks them back too.
Cobwebs slow whoever is in them: jump into one with a foe for crits, or stand in two to heal while they can't hit you.
Milk takes away every effect: poison from a cave spider, a witch's potions.
Phantoms come after three nights without sleep: sleep and they don't come.
